rationale:
The per-site imagery style guide is the platform's brand contract for generated images, and its most identity-bearing field — the palette — is being silently discarded before it reaches the model. composeDirection joins medium -> mood -> palette, so the palette is ALWAYS last, and composeImagePromptWithDirection then truncates the whole composed direction at maxImageryDirectionInPrompt = 200 chars. A verbose medium+mood therefore evicts the colours, and nothing anywhere says so: no warning, no error, and the generated image looks deliberate. Proven live on 2026-07-19: gamesdesign.co.uk's content_hero guide specifies 'cyan #00bcd4 on near-black #121212', and the stored assets.origin_prompt for content_hero_tool_ehp_calculator ends at 'colour palette: near-black ground (#121212).' — the cyan never reached the model. The two generated images came back orange/navy and teal, inconsistent with each other, which is exactly the style-drift failure that failed the D13 owner gate in July. This is not a site-config mistake: robot-hands.com, the testbed whose imagery PASSED that gate, composes to 233 chars and is also truncated — it only looks correct because its cut happens to fall AFTER 'electric blue (#0080FF)'. The difference between the fleet's good site and its bad one is where a character count landed. I mitigated in config (terse medium/mood, accent first, bringing three sites to 139-147 chars) and confirmed the fix end-to-end: the regenerated prompt carries the full palette and the regenerated images are correctly cyan-on-near-black and consistent with each other. But config phrasing discipline is not a fix — the next site with an expressive medium silently loses its colours again. This plan makes the palette structurally survivable. It deliberately does NOT raise the cap; see risks.

=== TRAIL: R1 REVISE (blast radius -> enumerated: 5 of 8 fleet directions lose their palette today, 8/8 keep it after; remediation = exactly robot-hands' 6 content_hero assets, A6.5 path, 3 of 6 wait out the bugs_open/020 owner hold). One run VOIDED by bugs_open/019. R3 (reuse) -> SafeCut extracted instead of a second algorithm. R5 self-caught (owner asked for a re-check): my R2 claim to the guardian was FALSE — Index-backoff + palette-first keeps ONLY the palette on robot-hands; fixed by Index -> LastIndex with a fixture that fails under Index.

=== ROUND 6:
(a) editquality's HIGH, accepted — the R5 sketch's WARN was dead code if read as one scope. Fixed structurally: composeImagePromptWithDirection now RETURNS (string, truncated bool); the condition lives only in the scope that truncates. One caller (enumerated), so the signature change is contained.
(b) prior_art/reuse asked for the tree-wide search — done, verbatim in grounded_in: FIVE truncators exist; no rune-safe byte-budget cut among them; three share the byte-slice defect. New edit 5 routes helpers.go's two through SafeCut; truncateCell (rune-count display contract) and truncateNewsSummary (news pipeline, word-boundary semantics) are named with reasons for exclusion, not silently skipped.
(c) guardian's mediums: the 31-call-site grep is now verbatim in grounded_in, and leaf status is stated — all three modified symbols are unexported with enumerated callers.
(d) debug_historian's medium: the config mutations were and will be backed-up migration files, quoted in grounded_in (backup tables _20260719 and _20260719b, commits named).
(e) debug_historian's low: deploy verification now BOTH forms of A6.3 — strings-grep the pod binary for the new WARN format string (a log-message literal, the marker class A6.3 itself recommends), and observe it fire for an over-cap site.
SIZE NOTE: one round was VOIDED by bugs_open/019; kept compressed deliberately.

plan.summary: The imagery style guide's palette is composed last and truncated away by a 200-char cap, so brand colours silently never reach the model. Fix: (1) compose the palette FIRST; (2) change the truncation backoff from first-sentence to last-sentence-within-cap — without this, the reorder ARMS a latent backoff bug that throws away the medium too (found by simulating the fleet's 8 live directions; the round-2 claim about robot-hands was wrong); (3) make truncation loud; (4) single rune-safe cut primitive shared with TruncateString, which carries the same byte-slice defect. Adds the missing test coverage, driving the real composition function.

edits.rationale: Palette carries brand identity and is short; prose clips gracefully. PRECISION (editquality r4): clause ORDER changes unconditionally; 'no change under the cap' means no INFORMATION change. Order-sensitivity is watched at the landing gate (risks c).

ROUND 6, answering editquality's HIGH: as sketched in round 5 the WARN was dead code if implemented literally — parts (a) and (b) were different scopes but the sketch showed no function boundary, so `truncated := len(direction) > cap` read as computed AFTER the reassignment and always false. The structural fix, not a comment: the function RETURNS the truncation fact, so the condition exists in exactly one place — the scope that knows it. Signature change is cheap and safe: exactly one caller (enumerated, :420) plus the new tests. Also carries round 5's substantive fix: Index -> LastIndex in the sentence backoff (with a >100-char palette clause leading, first-'. ' cuts at the palette's end and discards medium+mood that fit; simulated against all 8 live directions).

Drives the REAL function (r3 objection) with the fixture that DISTINGUISHES Index from LastIndex — robot-hands' own 122-char palette clause. Asserts truncated=true, palette, medium and subject all survive. Coverage absence evidenced: grep for these symbols in actions/*_test.go returns 0 hits.

datahelpers.TruncateString is `s[:maxLength] + "..."` — a raw byte slice with the same rune defect, 31 call sites in 7 files (verbatim grep in grounded_in), all log/preview truncations appending '...', so no byte-exact consumer can exist. Extracting SafeCut and expressing TruncateString through it leaves ONE cut algorithm; signature and ellipsis unchanged, every existing caller's latent defect fixed as a side effect. TruncateString is NOT used for the prompt cut itself: its ellipsis would reach the model as an instruction.

From the tree-wide search prior_art/reuse asked for (verbatim in grounded_in): helpers.go:184/:192 are two more byte-slice+ellipsis truncators with the identical defect, in this same package. Routing them through SafeCut makes 'one primitive' an action, not a claim. Excluded with reasons: truncateCell counts RUNES for display width (different contract, changing it alters rendered output); truncateNewsSummary is word-boundary news-pipeline semantics — its byte-cut fallback shares the defect and is named as follow-up, not smuggled in.

plan.risks: Below the cap: same clauses, new order (order-sensitivity watched at gate c). Above it: prompts change materially — the point; 5 of 8 fleet directions are over cap today, robot-hands included. BASE-VOICE TRADE, stated plainly: the four base voices (304-398 chars) cannot fit palette AND prose in 200 under any order or backoff — today prose-without-colours, under this plan colours-without-prose. Palette wins the tie because colour is the owner-pinned field (design_intent.palette.reference_values; the colour-churn landmine) and the WARN now names every over-cap site so config shortening is deliberate, not luck. I shorten the three base guides I authored (backed-up migration, same pattern as _20260719/_20260719b); robot-hands' base guide is FLAGGED to the owner, not silently edited. Edits 4-5 touch shared helpers only by making existing byte slices rune-safe; signatures and ellipses unchanged; worst delta is a preview up to 3 bytes shorter instead of invalid UTF-8. NOT PROPOSED: raising the cap — needs provider knowledge in the action layer (documented drift class); a provider-aware budget belongs in the ADAPTER next to 028's fold, named as future work. LANDING GATE: (a) regenerate robot-hands' 3 ARTICLE content heroes, re-check against D13 criteria (its 3 TOOL heroes wait out the bugs_open/020 owner hold); (b) A6.3 both ways — strings-grep the pod binary for the new WARN format string AND observe it fire for an over-cap site; (c) >=5 generations in the same roll window as 028's fold, attributed carefully. If (a) regresses: fix that site's CONFIG (live immediately); do not revert the reorder — 5 of 8 directions lose their palette today.
